translations.en: See decoded_fields. The 'B.' is Belgium/Brussels. The mother/father names and Cieszyn birthplace differ from family knowledge — explained by clerk's transcription error per the 15 May Nadwórna finding.
translations.he: ראה decoded_fields. ה'ב.' הוא בלגיה/בריסל. שמות ההורים ומקום הלידה צ'שין שונים מהידע המשפחתי — מוסבר כשגיאת תעתיק של פקיד לפי הממצא מ-15 במאי בנדבורנא.
translations.pl: Patrz decoded_fields. 'B.' to Belgia/Bruksela. Imiona rodziców i miejsce urodzenia Cieszyn różnią się od wiedzy rodzinnej — wyjaśnione jako błąd transkrypcji urzędnika zgodnie z odkryciem z 15 maja w Nadwórnej.
translations.fr: Voir decoded_fields. Le 'B.' est Belgique/Bruxelles. Les noms des parents et le lieu de naissance Cieszyn diffèrent de ce que connaît la famille — expliqué comme erreur de transcription du fonctionnaire, suite à la découverte du 15 mai à Nadwórna.

open_questions: Verify David's handwritten signature against any Israeli document (customs records?). Family has been unable to locate his English/Hebrew signature so far.
Decipher the stained note next to 1942 — 'deforce' (Belgian French for 'deprived') or 'déporté' (deported)?
Why did the clerk write 'Tesin'? Mishearing 'Nadwórna'? Or perhaps David himself misstated, given the political situation?

documents.source_archive: Bolechów Jewish vital records, AGAD Warsaw (former Eastern Borderlands collection) — gmina wyznaniowa Bolechów, powiat Dolina, księga metrykalna urodzeń 1907-1918

translations.en: Lea Weitzner, born 8 April 1913 in Bolechów. Father Elias Weitzner (cattle dealer), mother Matel née Weinreb. Given her name in the Bolechów synagogue on 12 April. Mother's parents: Samuel Weinreb (tavern keeper in Dolina) and Ester Blima. Elias and Matel married in Dolina, 1905 (statutory marriage).
translations.he: לאה וייצנר, נולדה 8 באפריל 1913 בבולוכוב. אב — אליהו וייצנר (סוחר בקר), אם — מתל לבית ויינרב. ניתן לה שם בבית הכנסת בבולוכוב ב-12 באפריל. הורי האם: שמואל ויינרב (בעל פונדק בדולינה) ואסתר בלימה. אליהו ומתל נישאו בדולינה ב-1905 (נישואין אזרחיים).
translations.pl: Lea Weitzner, urodzona 8 kwietnia 1913 w Bolechowie. Ojciec Elias Weitzner (handlarz bydłem), matka Matel z domu Weinreb. Imię nadane w synagodze w Bolechowie 12 kwietnia. Rodzice matki: Samuel Weinreb (karczmarz w Dolinie) i Ester Blima. Elias i Matel zawarli ślub w Dolinie w 1905 roku (małżeństwo statutowe).
translations.fr: Léa Weitzner, née le 8 avril 1913 à Bolechów. Père Elias Weitzner (marchand de bétail), mère Matel née Weinreb. Nommée à la synagogue de Bolechów le 12 avril. Parents de la mère : Samuel Weinreb (tavernier à Dolina) et Ester Blima. Elias et Matel se sont mariés à Dolina en 1905 (mariage civil).

title.he: רישום הוועד המרכזי של יהודי פולין — שמעון רפפורט (1937)
title.pl: Rejestracja CKŻP — Szymon Rapaport (1937)
title.fr: Enregistrement CKŻP — Szymon Rapaport (1937)

documents.source_archive: Central Committee of Polish Jews (Centralny Komitet Żydów w Polsce, CKŻP) — 'Karta informacyjna o osobach ocalałych' (information card on survivors), Wydział Ewidencji i Statystyki. Filed at Komitet Katowice, 1 July 1946. Card Nr 151337 (red index 2665). Now re-read from the full scan uploaded 18 May 2026 (upload aYoirGSgaPvA18H9qSAm).

translations.en: CKŻP survivor information card Nr 151337, filed at the Katowice committee on 1 July 1946. Surname Rappoport; given name Szymon; age/born 22.6.1937 in LWÓW (Lwów written in field 3 — NOT Mosina/Muszyna as family memory held); parents 'Dawid, Lusia'; last known address Katowice. The CKŻP collected names of Jewish survivors in Poland so families could find each other. The legible scan now establishes Lwów as Shimon's stated birthplace and 22.06.1937 as his DOB.
translations.he: כרטיס מידע על ניצול של הוועד המרכזי של יהודי פולין מס' 151337, הוגש בוועד קטוביץ ב-1 ביולי 1946. שם משפחה רפפורט; שם פרטי שמעון; גיל/נולד 22.6.1937 בלבוב (כתוב בשדה 3 — ולא מושינה/מוסינה כפי שזכרה המשפחה); הורים 'דוד, לוסיה'; כתובת אחרונה ידועה קטוביץ. הסריקה הקריאה קובעת כעת את לבוב כמקום הלידה המוצהר של שמעון ואת 22.06.1937 כתאריך לידתו.
translations.pl: Karta informacyjna CKŻP nr 151337, złożona w komitecie w Katowicach 1 lipca 1946. Nazwisko Rappoport; imię Szymon; wiek/urodzony 22.6.1937 we LWOWIE (w rubryce 3 — NIE Mosina/Muszyna, jak głosiła pamięć rodzinna); rodzice 'Dawid, Lusia'; ostatni znany adres Katowice. Czytelny skan ustala teraz Lwów jako podane miejsce urodzenia Szymona oraz 22.06.1937 jako datę urodzenia.
translations.fr: Fiche d'information CKŻP n° 151337, déposée au comité de Katowice le 1er juillet 1946. Nom Rappoport ; prénom Szymon ; âge/né le 22.6.1937 à LWÓW (champ 3 — et NON Mosina/Muszyna comme le voulait la mémoire familiale) ; parents « Dawid, Lusia » ; dernière adresse connue Katowice. Le scan lisible établit désormais Lwów comme lieu de naissance déclaré de Szymon et le 22.06.1937 comme date de naissance.

summary.en: Zygmunt Griffel was David Memek's first cousin once removed — son of Dawid Mendel Griffel Sr. (Rebeka's brother, Leizor Griffel's eldest son). This page establishes him as a major Galician-Jewish timber industrialist in 1934-35: 60,000 t/year to England, a five-port operation, with ambitions to brand Polish softwood. The 1938 Muszyna sawmill operating under 'Segal-Żupnik-Wilf' (per Rafał Żebrowski's Holocaust article) is identified in 1938 Przegląd Drzewny as a Zygmunt Griffel front company. Lusia's Muszyna hotel Willa Helin was in Zygmunt's sawmill town — the family-business ecosystem extended from Lwów-Gdynia exports down to Carpathian spa-town milling.

decoded_fields.document_1: Application for permission to travel abroad, Stanisławów 26 August 1924: 'I, the undersigned Berisch Rapaport, an industrialist residing in Stanisławów since 1918, declare that I am a citizen of the Republic of Poland of the Jewish faith, born in Radomyśl Wielki on July 30, 1886, in proof of which I have my ID card: Stanisławów, November 16, 1922 L/9376/22, and request the issuance of a foreign passport for travel to Vienna. Reason for travel: business.'
decoded_fields.document_2: Identity-card application, Stanisławów 27 January 1927: 'Bernard Rapaport, born July 30, 1886 in Radomyśl, son of Moses and [illegible mother]. Average height, average build, square face, black eyes, proportionate mouth, healthy teeth.'
decoded_fields.document_3: Reference docs: '1) Birth certificate dated 25 Feb 1916, Nos. 97. Volume V [illegible] 231 Sp 104. 2) Certificate of membership from Nadwórna 29 Jan 1927, no. 505/27.'

summary.en: DEFINITIVE PRIMARY DOCUMENT establishing Berisz / Bernard Rapaport's identity: born 30 July 1886 in Radomyśl Wielki, son of Moses, industrialist, resident of Stanisławów since 1918, address Kościuszki 4. Located by Basia at USHMM 25 May 2026; this is the source that corrected the earlier confusion with the Tarnów-1884 'Benzion' birth certificate (different family).

Five children all born in Radomyśl Wielki: Alte Leja (1882, m. Turkel, Vienna branch), Berish (1886, our line), Jente (1887), Freida Amalia (1888, d. Przemyśl 1942, descendants Nussbaum + Rosenfeld), Rebeka (1896, Austria).

summary.en: AUTHORITATIVE FAMILY TREE for the paternal Rapaport line: documents Moses Saul Rapaport as patriarch, his 5 children (all born Radomyśl Wielki), and their descendants including David Memek's first cousin Zwi Ayalon Nussbaum (b.1919 Przemyśl, survived to Israel d.2001 Haifa). The Turkel branch (Alte Leja's descendants) lived in Vienna; some perished in the Holocaust (Israel Menachem d.1942 Lwów; Siegfried d.1945 Belgium); others survived (Mordechai/Max d.1997, Rachel/Rosie d.1999).

summary.en: ⚠ NOT OUR FAMILY (most likely). This certificate of divorce, issued 16 September 1941 in Petach Tikvah, Mandatory Palestine, dissolves the marriage of Lea bat Shimon HaKohen Rapaport (age 29) and Michael Sigal (age 29, baker). Lea's father is named Shimon HaKohen Rapaport — but our paternal-line Shimon was a Griffel ancestor, not a Rapaport, and our Lusia (Lea Weitzner-Rapaport) was hiding in Lwów under the alias 'Maria Cizlik' in 1941. This Lea Rapaport (b. ~1912) is therefore a different person, from a different Rapaport-HaKohen rabbinical branch. The CC-Cohen patronymic suggests she may still be a distant cousin within the broader Rapoport-Kohen rabbinical dynasty, but no proximate link to our family has been established.

transcription_notes.en: UPDATE (Jun 2026): RECLASSIFIED as OUR FAMILY. This Lea is David Memek's first cousin — daughter of Szymon Rapaport (Berisz's brother). She married Michael/Yehiel Segal (this divorce), later remarried as Lea Fridman. The earlier 'not our family likely' verdict is withdrawn.

documents.source_archive: Israel State Archives (גנזך המדינה), Mandate Government series מ, file 3211/050. Government of Palestine, Department of Migration, HQ serial 90563. Arrived in the WhatsApp export of 7 July 2026 with no caption; identified 3 August 2026.

summary.en:
Read page by page on 3 August 2026. It is a Government of Palestine, Department of Migration file: APPLICATION FOR PALESTINIAN CITIZENSHIP, headquarters serial 90563, held by the Israel State Archives (גנזך המדינה) in the Mandate Government series מ, file 3211/050.

APPLICANT: NUSSBAUM, Hirsch Herman. Wife: Inge, maiden name Rosenbusch.

What the file states:
  • Applicant's Polish passport no. 118839, issued at PRZEMYŚL on 21 September 1938
  • Wife's German passport no. 94, issued at BORKEN on 10 July 1935
  • First entry into Palestine: 12 October 1938; immigrant registration HA/5934/B of the same date
  • Wife and children registered HA/4302/A on 22 August 1938
  • Marriage solemnised at HAIFA on 12 June 1941 — Haifa Jewish Community Rabbinical Office certificate H-49343 of 15 June 1941
  • A son, MORDECHAI YOSEF, born at Haifa on 25 April 1943 — certificate 1591/43 of 14 May 1943
  • Fee of 250 mils, receipt 715052 of 29 October 1945; application made at Haifa
  • Approved 29 November 1945; naturalisation certificate no. 48628
  • Both passports withdrawn at Haifa in 1946

WHY IT MATTERS, AND WHAT IS NOT YET PROVEN. Our tree holds Zwi (Hirsch) Nussbaum, born in Przemyśl in 1919 — father of Yehudit Shlomit Ayalon, the living cousin found in June 2026, who is named after Freida, Berisz's sister. Zwi is Hirsch. A Polish passport issued at Przemyśl in September 1938 fits a nineteen-year-old from that town leaving for Palestine, and he entered three weeks later.

That is a strong lead and it is NOT a proof. The pages read so far carry no birth date and no parents' names for the applicant, which are what would settle it. The wife here is Inge Rosenbusch and the recorded child is a son, Mordechai Yosef; we do not know the name of Yehudit Shlomit's mother. Nussbaum is not a rare name. He is therefore NOT attached to any person in the tree until the particulars page is read.

NEXT: the remaining pages of the file almost certainly carry the applicant's declaration with date and place of birth and his father's name. Reading those decides it either way.

decoded_fields.identification: CONFIRMED as the file of Zwi (Hirsch) Ayalon Nussbaum: the children listed are Mordekhai Yosef and YEHUDIT SHLOMIT, and Yehudit Shlomit Ayalon is the living cousin who reconnected with this family in June 2026. Birth particulars declared: Tarnów, 6 May 1919 — which conflicts with the Przemyśl birth register (7 May 1919) and is recorded rather than resolved.
decoded_fields.address_1946: 24 Hillel Street, Haifa — written in English on the applicant’s own declaration. An earlier reading of "34" from the Hebrew notice of January 1946 was mine and is withdrawn; the English form is the clearer hand.
decoded_fields.certificate_numbers: The certificate itself (p.19) is No. 47589, issued at Jerusalem on 25 January 1946 (כ״ג בשבט תש״ו), application serial 90563. The file summary and the receipt note (pp.4-5) both record the issued certificate as No. 48628. Both numbers are recorded as printed; no attempt is made here to reconcile them.
decoded_fields.passports_surrendered: Polish no. 118839 and wife’s German no. 94, surrendered at Haifa, 1946
decoded_fields.third_child_1946: RESOLVED. The "child born to applicant" reported by the Haifa Immigration Office on 14 May 1946 is YEHUDIT SHLOMIT herself, added by hand to the children’s table on the applicant’s own declaration (p.31): born at Haifa, April 1946. There is no third child. The applicant re-signed the amended form on 23 August 1946.
decoded_fields.wife_birth: Inge Rosenbusch, born Kassel, Germany, 3 July 1922; German nationality before marriage
decoded_fields.clerk_note: At the foot of the declaration: "1919 only acc. to ppt" — the clerk recording that the stated birth year rested on the passport alone. Relevant to the Tarnów/Przemyśl and 6/7 May conflict: the applicant may have been working from a passport rather than a certificate.
decoded_fields.supporters: Dr Gruber, physician, 15 Pevsner Street, Haifa; Dr Platner, pharmacist, Neveh Sha’anan — the two residents who vouched for the application
decoded_fields.photographs: Page 20 carries TWO MOUNTED PHOTOGRAPHS — Inge on the left, the applicant on the right. The form itself demanded them: "Three small photographs of applicant and of his wife if he is married should be furnished. Photomaton photographs will not be accepted." Both have been cropped out and attached to their person records. This is the only known photograph of Inge.
decoded_fields.yehudit_shlomit_birth: 25 April 1946 at Haifa — settled by the Ministry of the Interior confirmation of April 1996 bound into the file, which lists the wife and both children with places and dates. She and her brother share a birthday three years apart.
decoded_fields.ministry_confirmation_1996: State of Israel, Ministry of the Interior, Population Administration, Citizenship Department, ref 90563, dated 21 April 1996, signed Esther Migian, citizenship coordinator. It confirms the grant of Palestinian citizenship and lists those included: Inge (Kassel, Germany, 3.7.1922) wife; Mordekhai Yosef (Haifa, 25.4.1943) son; Yehudit Shlomit (Haifa, 25.4.1946) daughter. Someone requested this confirmation in 1996 — the same year a reader’s slip in the file shows the original being pulled from the State Archives.
decoded_fields.oath_signed: Oath of allegiance signed "Herman Nussbaum", 19 December 1945 (p.7; p.28 is the blank duplicate)
